description: "We used to look up at the sky and wonder at our place in the stars. Now we just look down, and worry about our place in the dirt." ~ Jospeph Cooper, Interstellar (2014)
summary:
AstroPulse is an offline, local-first health self-assessment prototype for astronaut crews. It combines daily check-ins with personal trend analysis, a body map, communication-blackout handling, and a local relay queue. Its dashboard compares readings with a crew member’s recent baseline and clearly shows status with an icon, text, and color. When communications are unavailable, entries stay queued locally; users decide whether to export a summary.

AstroPulse uses repeatable SIMULATED scenarios to demonstrate gradual changes, a temperature spike during a blackout, and changes in mood and exercise. It is designed to support awareness and communication during exploration missions, not to diagnose or direct medical care. Thresholds and generated values are placeholders, and source and safety reviews remain in progress.
details:
AstroPulse is a Django web app that runs locally and stores check-ins in SQLite. Users can record six indicators: resting heart rate, sleep, body temperature, mood and stress, exercise, and blood oxygen. The dashboard shows status against a recent personal baseline and configured limits, with reasons, trends, drift detection, and short-range forecasts. An interactive body map groups indicators by region. Environment profiles adjust which device-based prompts appear. During a communication blackout, the app queues items locally and supports an explicit export.

The prototype includes four repeatable simulated scenarios so reviewers can explore steady readings, gradual changes, a temperature spike during a blackout, and changes in mood and exercise. Demo readings are labeled SIMULATED. The app is built with Python 3.11+, Django, SQLite, NumPy, server-rendered templates, bundled HTMX and Plotly, and a locally stored 3D body model. It is designed to work without loading internet assets.

The project’s intended impact is to help crews notice changes in their own readings and organize information for follow-up, including when communication is delayed or unavailable. It keeps data on the device unless the user requests an export. AstroPulse is a research and demonstration prototype: its thresholds and simulated values are placeholders, sources are awaiting verification, and it is not a diagnostic or operational medical tool.
